newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela idled Amuay cracker to restart mid-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela idled Amuay cracker to restart mid-Nov.

text.p: Technical problems that downed a catalytic cracker at PdVSA affiliate Lagoven's 510,000 barrels per day (bpd) Amuay refinery early last week will be put to rights by the middle of November, Lagoven said.
"The unit will be back-up in three weeks, by the middle of November" a company spokesmen told Reuters.

Meanwhile supply contracts will be met from nearby refineries. "Maraven's Cordon refinery, Corpoven's El Palito, and the Isla refinery in Curacao will meet any shortfalls not covered by our inventories," the Lagoven spokesman said.
The spokesman added force majeure was "not contemplated".
Venezuela is the U.S.'s top foreign oil supplier shipping some 48,000 bpd of gasoline over the first half of the year, according to U.S. Department of Energy figures.
Amauy's 108,000 bpd cracker unit went down eight days ago after problems with an air compressor. The unit last failed in July, when international deliveries when met from reserves while it was fixed.
